home.ironAge.description: From furnace slag in Kodumanal to maritime beads at Poompuhar, our archaeology teams decode the Tamil Iron Age with lab-grade precision. faq.title: Frequently Asked Questions
faq.subtitle: Find answers to common questions about Meenkodi, our mission, and how you can get involved in preserving Tamil heritage.

items.question: What is Meenkodi?
items.answer: Meenkodi is a digital platform dedicated to preserving, documenting, and celebrating the rich cultural heritage of Tamil civilization. We aim to connect the global Tamil community with their roots through technology and storytelling.

items.question: Is Tamil one of the world's oldest civilizations?
items.answer: Yes, Tamil civilization is one of the world's oldest continuous civilizations, with documented history spanning over 2,000 years. Archaeological evidence from sites like Keeladi, Adichanallur, and Poompuhar suggests Tamil culture may extend back 3,000-4,000 years or more. The Tamil Brahmi script and Sangam literature provide concrete evidence of a sophisticated society dating to at least 300 BCE.

items.question: How old is the Tamil language?
items.answer: Tamil is one of the world's oldest living classical languages. It has a documented literary tradition of over 2,000 years, with the earliest Tamil-Brahmi inscriptions dating to around 500 BCE. Tamil is the only classical language that has maintained continuous literary production from ancient times to the present, making it unique among world languages.

items.question: What is Sangam literature?
items.answer: Sangam literature is a collection of ancient Tamil poems and texts composed between 300 BCE and 300 CE. It includes over 2,000 poems by more than 470 poets, covering themes of love, war, ethics, and daily life. Major works include Tolkappiyam (grammar), Ettuthokai (Eight Anthologies), and Pattupattu (Ten Idylls). This literature provides invaluable insights into ancient Tamil society, culture, and values.

items.question: What makes Tamil culture unique?
items.answer: Tamil culture is distinguished by its ancient literary tradition, classical language status, unique architectural achievements (like Dravidian temple architecture), rich performing arts (Bharatanatyam, Carnatic music), sophisticated philosophical systems, and the concept of 'Thinai' (landscape-based poetry). The culture has maintained remarkable continuity while adapting to modern times, preserving traditions in language, arts, festivals, and social customs.

items.question: What are Tamil contributions to world civilization?
items.answer: Tamil civilization has made significant contributions including: advanced maritime trade networks connecting Rome, Southeast Asia, and China; pioneering work in mathematics, astronomy, and medicine (Siddha system); architectural innovations in temple construction; classical dance and music traditions; philosophical texts like Thirukkural (translated into over 40 languages); and the development of one of the world's oldest grammatical treatises, Tolkappiyam.

items.question: What archaeological evidence exists for ancient Tamil civilization?
items.answer: Major archaeological sites include Keeladi (urban settlement from 600 BCE), Adichanallur (Iron Age burial site with 4,000-year-old artifacts), Poompuhar (ancient port city mentioned in Sangam literature), Arikamedu (Roman trade settlement), and numerous megalithic sites. Excavations have revealed Tamil-Brahmi inscriptions, pottery, jewelry, tools, and urban planning evidence that confirm the antiquity and sophistication of Tamil civilization.
